authoredNote: The expected lines were TRANSCRIBED from a measured run of this fixture through the production entry and checked line by line against the source (`cat -n`) — they record what the analyzer does, not what it ought to. What makes them constraints rather than a snapshot is the forbid set: every entry there is an independently-argued construct-start position that Rust parses (a call chain broken before the dot, a plain field access broken the same way, wrapped supertrait bounds, a wrapped trait reference in an impl header), so the fixture fails if the analyzer moves to any of them.
rationale: M59.A7 (#825). Rust emitted NO line_number on any relationship before this pin — measured through the production entry on a 200-file draw of cargo+ripgrep: 0 of 65,390 edges lined, now 65,390/65,390 lined with 0 fabricated zeros and 0 lines outside their file. The pre-fix state is therefore 'unlined', and the traps below are the ways a rust line can be PRESENT and still wrong, each valid Rust and each measured on this fixture before being written down: (1) a call chain BROKEN BEFORE THE DOT — `repo` + newline + `.find(1)` parses, a `field_expression` starts at its VALUE, so the callee leaf is one and two lines later than the construct start; (2) the same shape as a plain FIELD ACCESS (`self` / `.items` / `.len()` on three lines); (3) wrapped SUPERTRAIT BOUNDS, where the bound's own line is the site and the `trait` keyword line is not; (4) a wrapped TRAIT REFERENCE in an impl header, where the edge names the trait written after `impl`; (5) a `Self`-returning signature, where the target is the enclosing type that the source writes only as the keyword `Self`. The one residual this fixture cannot pin is the `Self`-resolution CLASS itself, which the M59 oracle now reports in its notCheckable bucket with a per-file sample and reason (21 of 65,390 claims, all on correct lines: `-> Self`, `-> Result<Self, D::Error>`, `&mut Self`, `Self { .. }`).
